question: Why did the authors choose copper current collectors for the anode-free sodium cell?

trace.query: SELECT id, page, text FROM lines WHERE text ILIKE '%copper%' OR text ILIKE '%Cu %' OR text ILIKE '%Cu)%' OR text ILIKE '%Cu,%' OR text ILIKE '%Cu-%'
SELECT id, page, text FROM atoms WHERE text ILIKE '%copper%' OR text ILIKE '%Cu foil%' OR text ILIKE '%Cu current%'

SELECT id, page, line_no, text FROM lines WHERE page IN (2,3) AND (text ILIKE '%Cu%' OR text ILIKE '%Al %' OR text ILIKE '%hysteresis%' OR text ILIKE '%cheaper%' OR text ILIKE '%weight%') ORDER BY page, line_no

runs.text: The document does not say that the authors chose copper current collectors. They chose aluminum. The paper states that Al was selected instead of Cu, and gives the reason as its lower cost and lower weight, both advantages for sodium-based chemistries:

runs.quote: Cu because it offers significant cost (∼3× cheaper) and weight

runs.text: (the rest of that line reads as a weight benefit of the same kind). Copper appears only once more, as a point of comparison: prior work using Cu electrodes reported nearly double the voltage hysteresis of the carbon/Al electrodes at high current.

runs.quote: using Cu electrodes reported nearly double the hysteresis at

runs.text: . The anode-free cell therefore uses carbon-coated Al current collectors, not copper.
